Goal: Session Manager usage dashboard ignores scheduler.job.finish — the one event that measures orchestration

Finding from the Session Manager desktop app (~/Projects/session-manager), which is the client that POSTs to this site's /api/telemetry/* beacons.

**Symptom.** The admin usage rollup at `server/routes/admin-session-manager-usage.ts` aggregates exactly three event names:

```
const EV_LAUNCH  = 'app.launch';
const EV_SESSION = 'session.open';
const EV_EPIC    = 'epic.create';
```

The desktop client emits a fourth counter — `scheduler.job.finish`, carrying `props.status` (one of `completed` / `failed` / `needs_review`) — from `src/main/lib/telemetryCounters.cjs` in the Session Manager repo. It is ingested fine (POST /api/telemetry/event writes it into `funnel_events` with `event='scheduler.job.finish'`, `tool='session-manager'`), but nothing on this side ever reads it back out, so it is invisible in the dashboard.

**Why it matters.** `scheduler.job.finish` is the only signal that measures whether the product's core loop — queueing PRDs and having headless jobs actually run them — works on other people's machines. Launches and epic creations tell you people opened the app; job finishes (and especially the failed/needs_review ratio) tell you whether the orchestration succeeds for them. A fleet where every install launches, creates epics, and never finishes a job looks healthy under the current query.

**What we'd expect.** The `usageDaily` and `usageByVersion` queries extended with per-status job counts, e.g.:

```sql
SUM(CASE WHEN event = 'scheduler.job.finish' AND json_extract(metadata,'$.status') = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS jobsCompleted,
SUM(CASE WHEN event = 'scheduler.job.finish' AND json_extract(metadata,'$.status') = 'failed'    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS jobsFailed,
...
```

plus a job success-rate line in the admin page that renders this payload. `props.status` is already stored in the `metadata` blob by the ingest route (`safeMeta(e.props, ...)`), so no client or ingest change is needed — this is a read-side-only change.

**One caveat, so you don't act on bad numbers yet.** As of 2026-09-12 no real usage data has been delivered from our side at all — the client has never successfully flushed (no `telemetry-sent.json` on the dev machine, `lastDailyFlushAt` null), and the spooled records are dominated by test artefacts. That is being fixed in the Session Manager repo (PRDs 1166 and its follow-up). So build the query, but treat any currently-present `session-manager` rows in `funnel_events` as untrustworthy until that lands.

Suspected file in your repo: `server/routes/admin-session-manager-usage.ts`, plus whichever admin page component consumes `/api/admin/session-manager/usage` (`src/pages/AdminPage.tsx` or a child under `src/pages/admin/`).
